questions.stem: Crossing a bar with a heavy swell, the best time is usually:
options: At night when breakers are less visible
At low water with the stream running out
Near high water slack, if the bar is safe at that time
At the strongest part of the ebb
questions.rationale: Swell steepens as depth reduces; a falling tide against swell is worst.

questions.stem: Neap tides occur:
options: Near new moon and full moon
When the Moon is closest to the Earth
Near the first and last quarters of the Moon
Only around the equinoxes
questions.rationale: At the quarters the Sun and Moon act at right angles, so the range is smallest.

questions.stem: Backing wind means the wind direction is changing:
options: Towards the east
In speed only
Anticlockwise
Clockwise
questions.rationale: Backing = anticlockwise; veering = clockwise.

questions.stem: A sailing vessel with the wind on her port side sees a vessel to windward and cannot tell her tack. She shall:
options: Tack at once
Sound five blasts and stand on
Stand on
Keep out of the way
questions.rationale: Rule 12(a)(iii): she shall keep out of the way of that vessel.

questions.stem: True course 265°. Variation 5°W. Deviation 1°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 5° (W variation) = 270°. Magnetic to compass: add 1° (W deviation) = 271°.

questions.stem: A running fix will be unreliable if:
options: The interval is short
The bearings are 90° apart
Tide and leeway between the bearings are not allowed for
Both bearings are taken from lighthouses
questions.rationale: Errors in course, distance, stream or leeway affect the transferred line.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 2145. The secondary port time difference for HW is +35 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 2145 +35 min = 2220.

questions.stem: True bearing 250°, variation 6°E. The magnetic bearing is:
questions.rationale: Magnetic = true − east variation = 250 − 6. Answer: 244°.

questions.stem: An activated EPIRB:
options: Sends a VHF message to nearby ships on channel 16 only
Transmits a distress alert via satellite with identity and position
Switches on all the navigation lights on the boat
Provides a weather forecast for the area to the crew
questions.rationale: A 406 MHz beacon alerts rescue centres. Answer: Transmits a distress alert via satellite with identity and position.

questions.stem: The 'duration' of a tide in the almanac is the time between:
options: Moonrise and moonset on the day
Successive HW and LW, usually about 6 h 12 min
Successive HW at springs and neaps
HW and the next HW, about 12 h 25 min
questions.rationale: Duration is the interval between HW and LW (or LW and HW).

questions.stem: In open water, a sailing vessel and a vessel engaged in fishing are on courses that involve risk of collision. A sailing vessel is not overtaking. Which vessel keeps out of the way?
options: A vessel engaged in fishing
The larger vessel
The faster vessel
A sailing vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 18 hierarchy: NUC, then RAM, then fishing, then sailing, then power-driven. A lower-ranked vessel keeps out of the way of a higher-ranked one.

questions.stem: In a narrow channel, two prolonged then one short blast means:
options: I am in distress
I am turning round
I intend to overtake you on your port side
I intend to overtake you on your starboard side
questions.rationale: Rule 34(c)(i) says: I intend to overtake you on your starboard side.

questions.stem: The warm sector of a depression lies between:
options: The centre of the low and the warm front
The warm front and the cold front
The cold front and the centre of the low
The warm front and the high
questions.rationale: Warm sector weather is often low cloud and drizzle.

questions.stem: You see three all-round red lights in a vertical line at night. The vessel is:
options: A vessel engaged in mine clearance
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel at anchor under 50 m
A vessel constrained by her draught
questions.rationale: Rule 28: three all-round red lights in a vertical line indicates a vessel constrained by her draught.

questions.stem: A rhumb line is:
options: A line crossing all meridians at the same angle
A line of equal pressure
The shortest distance between two points
A line of equal depth
questions.rationale: A rhumb line is a path of constant true bearing; it is straight on a Mercator chart.

questions.stem: A tow exceeding 200 m shows by day:
options: A black ball where it can best be seen
Two black cones, points together
A diamond where it can best be seen
A black cylinder where it can best be seen
questions.rationale: Rule 24(a)(v) and (c) says: A diamond where it can best be seen.

questions.stem: A sector light's white sector usually marks:
options: A wreck
The safe approach channel
The edge of the shipping lane
An area of fog
questions.rationale: Coloured sectors warn of dangers. Answer: The safe approach channel.

questions.stem: If in doubt whether you are overtaking another vessel, you shall:
options: Sound five short blasts and then stand on
Assume you are overtaking and act accordingly
Assume you are in a crossing situation
Assume you are the stand-on vessel here
questions.rationale: Rule 13(d): if in doubt, assume you are overtaking and keep clear.

questions.stem: A bank dries 1.8 m. Your draught is 1.2 m and you want 1.0 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.2 + 1.0 = 2.2 m; add the drying height 1.8 m = 4.0 m.

questions.stem: What does a power-driven vessel under 50 m underway show? (night)
options: Masthead light, sidelights and sternlight
Three all-round green lights
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
Green over white all-round lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 23: a power-driven vessel under 50 m underway shows masthead light, sidelights and sternlight.

questions.stem: VHF channel 70 is used for:
options: Calls to marinas
Weather broadcasts
Digital selective calling only
Voice distress calls
questions.rationale: No voice on 70. Answer: Digital selective calling only.

questions.stem: A gale warning is issued when the mean wind is expected to reach at least:
options: Force 10
Force 8
Force 6
Force 7
questions.rationale: A strong wind warning is force 6 or 7; gale warning force 8 or gusts of 43–51 knots.

questions.stem: A sailing vessel under 20 m may combine her sidelights and sternlight in:
options: A red all-round light at the masthead
A masthead light with sidelights
A tricolour lantern at or near the masthead
Two green lights
questions.rationale: Rule 25(b) says: A tricolour lantern at or near the masthead.

questions.stem: TCPA means:
options: Time to closest point of approach
Total course plotted angle
Tidal current position average
Time of chart position accuracy
questions.rationale: TCPA is the time until CPA occurs. Answer: Time to closest point of approach.

questions.stem: A west cardinal mark has:
options: Two cones point to point, yellow with a black band
Two cones base to base, black with a yellow band
Two cones pointing down, yellow over black
Two cones pointing up, black over yellow
questions.rationale: West: point to point, like a wine glass. Answer: Two cones point to point, yellow with a black band.

questions.stem: You see three black balls in a vertical line by day. The vessel is:
options: A vessel constrained by her draught
A vessel aground
A vessel at anchor
A vessel engaged in fishing
questions.rationale: Rule 30(d): three black balls in a vertical line indicates a vessel aground.

questions.stem: A bank dries 0.9 m. Your draught is 1.4 m and you want 0.5 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.4 + 0.5 = 1.9 m; add the drying height 0.9 m = 2.8 m.

questions.stem: Compass course 190°. Deviation 5°W. Variation 5°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: subtract 5° = 185°. Magnetic to true: subtract 5° = 180°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: A depth contour can be used for pilotage by:
options: Using a fixed course for the contour
Following a chosen depth with the echo sounder
Staying in water deeper than the contour at all times
Ignoring the echo sounder
questions.rationale: Following a contour keeps a safe distance off.

questions.stem: You see two all-round red lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights and sternlight at night. The vessel is:
options: A vessel engaged in mine clearance
A vessel at anchor under 50 m
A fishing vessel, not trawling
A vessel not under command, making way
questions.rationale: Rule 27(a): two all-round red lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights and sternlight indicates a vessel not under command, making way.

questions.stem: Which seabed is best for drying out a bilge-keel or fin-keel yacht?
options: Firm, level sand or gravel, free of rocks
Weed-covered shingle with large boulders
A rock ledge with a pool of water
Soft deep mud with a steep slope
questions.rationale: Check the bottom, slope and shelter in advance.

questions.stem: A safe-water mark is:
options: Red and white vertical stripes, with a red sphere
Black and red horizontal bands, with two spheres
Yellow with an X topmark
Green with a red band
questions.rationale: Safe water all around, such as a fairway or mid-channel.

questions.stem: In fog, a sailing vessel underway sounds, every 2 minutes:
options: One prolonged and two short blasts
Three prolonged blasts in quick succession
Two prolonged blasts in quick succession
Three short blasts in quick succession
questions.rationale: Rule 35(c): one prolonged followed by two short. The same signal is used by NUC, RAM, constrained, fishing and towing vessels.

questions.stem: A bilge pump set-up should include:
options: A single electric pump under the cabin sole
Two pumps wired on the same circuit and switch
At least two independent pumps, one operable from the cockpit
A bucket and a sponge kept in the cockpit locker
questions.rationale: Redundancy ensures one pump is available. Answer: At least two independent pumps, one operable from the cockpit.

questions.stem: Crew briefing before departure should include:
options: The names of other boats in the marina
Safety equipment, MOB procedure and the passage plan
The route taken on previous trips
The cost of the harbour dues
questions.rationale: A good briefing speeds up the response in an emergency.

questions.stem: You can tell an anchor is dragging when:
options: Another boat arrives and anchors near by
The boat swings round with the wind or the tide
Transit marks or the GPS show you moving over the ground
The tide turns and the stream changes direction
questions.rationale: Use transits and anchor alarms. Answer: Transit marks or the GPS show you moving over the ground.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 1705. The secondary port time difference for HW is +25 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 1705 +25 min = 1730.

questions.stem: A vessel engaged in mine clearance shows:
options: Three all-round green lights
A flashing blue light
Three all-round red lights
Two all-round green lights
questions.rationale: Rule 27(f): danger exists to other vessels within 1000 m.

questions.stem: An east cardinal mark has:
options: Two cones pointing down, yellow over black
Two cones point to point, yellow with a black band
Two cones pointing up, black over yellow
Two cones base to base, black with a yellow band
questions.rationale: East: base to base. Answer: Two cones base to base, black with a yellow band.

questions.stem: Which should be considered first before deciding to start a passage?
options: The brand and model of the GPS fitted to the boat
The availability of a berth ashore at the end of the trip
The weather forecast for the whole passage plus a margin
The colour of the spinnaker and the state of the sails
questions.rationale: A forecast covering the passage and a margin is vital.

questions.stem: Cirrus clouds are:
options: High, wispy clouds of ice crystals
Low clouds in contact with the sea
Low grey layer clouds
Dense towering rain clouds
questions.rationale: Cirrus often precede a warm front. Answer: High, wispy clouds of ice crystals.

questions.stem: Dead reckoning (DR) uses:
options: Course steered and tidal stream only
Compass bearings of charted objects
Course made good and distance over the ground
Course steered and distance run through the water
questions.rationale: DR ignores tide and leeway. Answer: Course steered and distance run through the water.

questions.stem: A vertical sextant angle of a charted object of known height gives:
options: The bearing of the object
The tidal stream rate
The distance off the object
The depth at the position
questions.rationale: Distance = height ÷ tan(angle). Answer: The distance off the object.

questions.stem: Compass course 165°. Deviation 2°W. Variation 5°E. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: subtract 2° = 163°. Magnetic to true: add 5° = 168°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: A bank dries 1.2 m. Your draught is 2.0 m and you want 1.0 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 2.0 + 1.0 = 3.0 m; add the drying height 1.2 m = 4.2 m.

questions.stem: You see anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights in a vertical line at night. The vessel is:
options: A vessel constrained by her draught
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A fishing vessel, not trawling
A vessel aground, under 50 m
questions.rationale: Rule 30(d): anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights in a vertical line indicates a vessel aground, under 50 m.

questions.stem: Before sailing, the plan and expected arrival should be left with:
options: Nobody at all, to avoid causing a false alarm
The nearest harbour office only, in case of delay
A responsible person ashore, with instructions if you are overdue
Any other vessel berthed in the marina at the time
questions.rationale: Shore contact tells the coastguard when to raise the alarm.

questions.stem: A deviation card gives deviation:
options: For different speeds
For different latitudes
For different times of year
For different headings of the yacht
questions.rationale: A card is made by swinging the compass. Answer: For different headings of the yacht.

questions.stem: LW height 1.0 m, HW height 6.4 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 5 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 5.4 m. After 5 h, 11/12 of the range has risen = 4.95 m. Height = 1.0 + 4.95 = 5.95 m.

questions.stem: A safety harness line should be clipped to:
options: A strong point, such as a jackstay or deck eye
A guardrail stanchion near the cockpit
A cockpit cushion lashed to the seat
A winch handle fitted to a primary winch
questions.rationale: Stanchions and rails can fail under load. Answer: A strong point, such as a jackstay or deck eye.

questions.stem: What does a sailing vessel also using her engine show? (day)
options: A black cylinder
Two black cones with their points together
A black cone, point down, forward
Two black balls in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 25(e): a sailing vessel also using her engine shows a black cone, point down, forward.

questions.stem: Close isobars on a weather chart indicate:
options: Strong winds
Light winds
A front
Fog
questions.rationale: A steep pressure gradient means a strong gradient wind.

questions.stem: At 4.0 kn over the ground, how long to cover 12 NM?
options: 2 h 24 min
4 h 00 min
3 h 00 min
0 h 20 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 12 ÷ 4.0 = 3.00 h = 3 h 00 min.

questions.stem: A vessel not under command shows at night:
options: Three red all-round lights in a vertical line
Red over white over red all-round lights
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
Green over white all-round lights in a line
questions.rationale: Rule 27(a) says: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: A sea breeze is usually strongest:
options: At dawn
Just before sunrise
At midnight
In mid to late afternoon
questions.rationale: The land-sea temperature difference is greatest in the afternoon.

questions.stem: At night you see a vessel's green sidelight on your starboard bow, bearing steady, range closing. She and you are both power-driven. You should:
options: Sound one short blast and hold course
Turn to port across her bow
Hold course and speed as the stand-on vessel
Keep out of the way, avoiding crossing ahead of her
questions.rationale: A green light is her starboard side, so you have her on your starboard side and must give way (Rule 15).

questions.stem: What does a vessel engaged in mine clearance show? (night)
options: Three all-round green lights
Red over white all-round lights in a vertical line
One all-round white light
White over red all-round lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 27(f): a vessel engaged in mine clearance shows three all-round green lights.

questions.stem: LW height 0.8 m, HW height 6.2 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 4 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 5.4 m. After 4 h, 9/12 of the range has risen = 4.05 m. Height = 0.8 + 4.05 = 4.85 m.

questions.stem: A typical recreational GPS receiver in good conditions is accurate to within:
options: About a nautical mile
A few miles
A few hundred metres
A few metres
questions.rationale: Typical accuracy is within 3–10 m, but errors still occur.

questions.stem: A passage plan should be updated:
options: Whenever conditions change significantly
Only after arrival
Once a week
Only if the destination changes
questions.rationale: Monitoring includes revisiting the plan. Answer: Whenever conditions change significantly.

questions.stem: Compass course 230°. Deviation 1°W. Variation 1°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: subtract 1° = 229°. Magnetic to true: subtract 1° = 228°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: During a MOB, one crew member should be told to:
options: Prepare hot drinks and blankets in the cabin
Point at the casualty continuously
Take photographs of the casualty for the report
Collect the safety gear and stow it below
questions.rationale: Losing sight of the casualty greatly reduces the chance of recovery.

questions.stem: True course 275°. Variation 3°E. Deviation 1°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: subtract 3° (E variation) = 272°. Magnetic to compass: add 1° (W deviation) = 273°.

questions.stem: Stratus clouds are:
options: Towering clouds with anvil tops and heavy showers
Low, grey layer clouds that may produce drizzle
High wispy clouds made of ice crystals, high in the sky
Heaped clouds with flat bases and rounded tops by day
questions.rationale: Stratus is a low uniform layer. Answer: Low, grey layer clouds that may produce drizzle.

questions.stem: A depth alarm should be set to:
options: Zero
The charted depth of the harbour
Off while in port
A depth based on draught and a safe margin
questions.rationale: Allow for tide and swell. Answer: A depth based on draught and a safe margin.

questions.stem: True course 135°. Variation 6°W. Deviation 3°E. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 6° (W variation) = 141°. Magnetic to compass: subtract 3° (E deviation) = 138°.

questions.stem: Five or more short rapid blasts mean:
options: I am in distress and need assistance now
I doubt your intentions or that you are taking enough action
I am altering course and turning round
I wish to overtake you on your port side
questions.rationale: Rule 34(d): the doubt or danger signal says: I doubt your intentions or that you are taking enough action.

questions.stem: An overtaken vessel agreeing to be overtaken sounds:
options: Prolonged, short, prolonged, short
Two short blasts in succession
Five short and rapid blasts
Three short blasts in succession
questions.rationale: Rule 34(c)(ii) says: Prolonged, short, prolonged, short.

questions.stem: To set an anchor correctly you:
options: Drop it from speed
Lower it and reverse slowly to dig it in
Raise it and drop again
Leave it on the bottom without pulling
questions.rationale: Backing down sets the anchor. Answer: Lower it and reverse slowly to dig it in.

questions.stem: The characteristic Oc 10s means:
options: A single flash every 10 seconds
Equal light and dark, repeating every 10 seconds
More light than dark, repeating every 10 seconds
Ten flashes in every minute
questions.rationale: Occulting lights are on for longer than they are off.

questions.stem: The stand-on vessel may first act on her own when:
options: She has made one short blast to the other
She first sees the other vessel approaching
It becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not acting appropriately
The range between them falls below three miles
questions.rationale: Rule 17(a)(ii): the stand-on vessel may take action as soon as it becomes apparent that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action.

questions.stem: Wind against tide produces:
options: A shorter period swell only
Lower waves
Smoother, longer waves
Steeper, more breaking waves
questions.rationale: Steeper waves are more dangerous for small craft.

questions.stem: An anemometer measures:
options: Air humidity
Wind speed
Atmospheric pressure
Sea temperature
questions.rationale: A vane shows wind direction. Answer: Wind speed.

questions.stem: The 'stand' of the tide is:
options: The period of the fastest rise or fall of the tide
The time between springs and the following neaps
The period around HW or LW when the height hardly changes
The moment when the tidal stream reverses direction
questions.rationale: Ports with a long stand include Southampton (at HW).

questions.stem: Under Rule 36, signals to attract attention must:
options: Be a red flare fired in the direction of danger
Be a flashing blue light directed at the vessel
Not be capable of being mistaken for any authorised signal
Be five short and rapid blasts on the whistle
questions.rationale: Rule 36 says: Not be capable of being mistaken for any authorised signal.

questions.stem: One short blast means:
options: I am altering my course to port
I am operating astern propulsion
I am altering my course to starboard
I intend to overtake you
questions.rationale: Rule 34(a): one short blast = altering to starboard.

questions.stem: A liferaft should be stowed:
options: Lashed inside the cabin, ready to carry up
In the cockpit locker with the fenders and warps
Deep in a locker under the saloon berth
Where it can be launched quickly, preferably with a hydrostatic release
questions.rationale: Quick access and release matter. Answer: Where it can be launched quickly, preferably with a hydrostatic release.

questions.stem: You see a vessel's green sidelight on your starboard bow. She is:
options: On a head-on course
Crossing from your port side; you stand on
Crossing from your starboard side; you give way
Overtaking you
questions.rationale: A green sidelight is her starboard side, so she is showing you her starboard side; you have her on your starboard bow and you keep clear if risk exists.

questions.stem: LW height 1.5 m, HW height 7.5 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 4 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 6.0 m. After 4 h, 9/12 of the range has risen = 4.50 m. Height = 1.5 + 4.50 = 6.00 m.

questions.stem: True course 015°. Variation 8°W. Deviation 3°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 8° (W variation) = 023°. Magnetic to compass: add 3° (W deviation) = 026°.

questions.stem: At 5.5 kn, the distance covered in 3 hours 30 minutes is:
A trip line on an anchor is attached to:
options: The mast, with a block
The chain shackle, with the windlass
The stock of the anchor, with a cleat on board
The crown of the anchor, with a buoy at the surface
questions.rationale: It frees a fouled anchor. Answer: The crown of the anchor, with a buoy at the surface.

questions.stem: A funnelling effect strengthens wind:
options: In the lee of a headland, close to the shore
Over a wide, flat bay with no high ground around it
In the open sea, well away from any high land
Between high land masses or through a strait
questions.rationale: Gaps channel the airflow and increase speed. Answer: Between high land masses or through a strait.

questions.stem: A Pan-Pan call is used for:
options: A vessel that is sinking and the crew are abandoning her
A routine radio check with a nearby marina or yacht
A person in the water in rough sea and getting colder
An urgent situation that is not immediate danger to life
questions.rationale: Pan-Pan precedes an urgency message. Answer: An urgent situation that is not immediate danger to life.

questions.stem: A bank dries 0.9 m. Your draught is 1.8 m and you want 0.5 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.8 + 0.5 = 2.3 m; add the drying height 0.9 m = 3.2 m.

questions.stem: Charted depth is 3.0 m and the height of tide is 2.0 m. The depth of water is:
questions.rationale: Depth = charted depth + height of tide. Answer: 5.0 m.

questions.stem: A log reads 125.4 at 1000 and 138.2 at 1230. The speed through the water is:
options: 4.8 knots
5.1 knots
5.8 knots
6.2 knots
questions.rationale: 12.8 NM in 2.5 h = 5.12 kn. Answer: 5.1 knots.

questions.stem: LW height 1.2 m, HW height 4.8 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 4 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 3.6 m. After 4 h, 9/12 of the range has risen = 2.70 m. Height = 1.2 + 2.70 = 3.90 m.

questions.stem: HW height 4.8 m, LW 0.6 m. By the Rule of Twelfths, the height 1 hour after HW is:
questions.rationale: Range 4.2 m; the first hour of fall is 1/12 = 0.35 m; height = 4.8 − 0.35 = 4.45 m.

questions.stem: True course 325°. Variation 6°E. Deviation 1°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: subtract 6° (E variation) = 319°. Magnetic to compass: add 1° (W deviation) = 320°.

questions.stem: Compass course 030°. Deviation 3°E. Variation 4°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: add 3° = 033°. Magnetic to true: subtract 4° = 029°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: Beaufort force 10 is:
options: Gale, 34 to 40 knots
Violent storm, 56 to 63 knots
Storm, 48 to 55 knots
Severe gale, 41 to 47 knots
questions.rationale: Force 9 is severe gale; 11 violent storm. Answer: Storm, 48 to 55 knots.

questions.stem: In strengthening winds you should plan to keep:
options: Close inshore for shelter from the swell and the wind
Directly along a lee shore so as to stay in shallow water
Sea room and an escape route to windward
Inside the outer buoys of a harbour, whatever the entrance
questions.rationale: Sea room is the primary safety margin. Answer: Sea room and an escape route to windward.

questions.stem: For harbour entry details, local rules and hazards you would consult:
options: The tidal stream atlas
The logbook of the previous trip
The pilot book or almanac
The shipping forecast
questions.rationale: Pilot books and almanacs give approach details and local information.

questions.stem: Corrections to charts are published in:
options: Reeds Almanac Tidal Stream Atlas
The Nautical Almanac
Admiralty Tide Tables
Notices to Mariners
questions.rationale: Apply corrections up to date before use. Answer: Notices to Mariners.

questions.stem: A 'tidal gate' is a place where:
options: The tide must be favourable or deep enough to pass safely
A tidal stream always runs at its maximum rate
A harbour barrier closes automatically at high water
A buoy marks the entrance to a buoyed channel
questions.rationale: Planning around tidal gates fixes your departure time.

questions.stem: In open water, a vessel engaged in fishing and a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre are on courses that involve risk of collision. A vessel engaged in fishing is not overtaking. Which vessel keeps out of the way?
options: A vessel engaged in fishing
The faster vessel
The larger vessel
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
questions.rationale: Rule 18 hierarchy: NUC, then RAM, then fishing, then sailing, then power-driven. A lower-ranked vessel keeps out of the way of a higher-ranked one.

questions.stem: In a narrow channel, a vessel shall avoid anchoring:
options: Under any circumstances whatever
If the circumstances of the case admit
During hours of daylight only
Unless she carries two anchors
questions.rationale: Rule 9(g) says: If the circumstances of the case admit.

questions.stem: If you run aground on a rising tide, you should:
options: Abandon ship at once
Run the engine at full power
Open the seacocks to cool the engine
Reduce draught or kedge off, then check for damage
questions.rationale: Use the rising tide to refloat if safe. Answer: Reduce draught or kedge off, then check for damage.

questions.stem: A clearing bearing in pilotage is:
options: A bearing of the stream taken from the almanac
A bearing taken from the compass rose on the chart
A bearing that must not be exceeded or reduced to remain clear of a danger
A bearing taken from a pair of objects to get a fix
questions.rationale: Draw it on the chart in advance. Answer: A bearing that must not be exceeded or reduced to remain clear of a danger.

questions.stem: LW height 0.8 m, HW height 3.8 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 2 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 3.0 m. After 2 h, 3/12 of the range has risen = 0.75 m. Height = 0.8 + 0.75 = 1.55 m.

questions.stem: NAVTEX broadcasts navigational and weather warnings on:
options: 2182 kHz, as voice
VHF channel 16, as voice
518 kHz, as text printed on board
VHF channel 70, as digital calls
questions.rationale: NAVTEX is an automated text service. Answer: 518 kHz, as text printed on board.

questions.stem: The 'range' of a tide is:
options: The difference in height between HW and the adjacent LW
The time between HW and the following LW
The height of HW above chart datum
The distance the tide runs up a river
questions.rationale: Range = height of HW − height of LW. Answer: The difference in height between HW and the adjacent LW.

questions.stem: LW height 0.4 m, HW height 5.8 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 2 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 5.4 m. After 2 h, 3/12 of the range has risen = 1.35 m. Height = 0.4 + 1.35 = 1.75 m.

questions.stem: True course 210°. Variation 3°W. Deviation 2°E. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 3° (W variation) = 213°. Magnetic to compass: subtract 2° (E deviation) = 211°.

questions.stem: What does a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre show? (day)
options: Ball, diamond, ball in a vertical line
Three black balls in a vertical line
A black cylinder
A diamond on tug and tow
questions.rationale: Rule 27(b): a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shows ball, diamond, ball in a vertical line.

questions.stem: Many harbours require you to call the authority on VHF:
options: Only after you are berthed, to report your arrival
Before entering, on the channel stated in the pilot book
Only if you are over 20 m, since small boats are exempt
On channel 16 during fog only, for safety reasons
questions.rationale: Follow local instructions. Answer: Before entering, on the channel stated in the pilot book.

questions.stem: Charted soundings (depths) are measured:
options: Below mean high water
Above mean sea level
Above lowest astronomical tide
Below chart datum
questions.rationale: A sounding is the depth of water below chart datum at that point.

questions.stem: A south cardinal mark has the topmark:
options: Two cones point to point
Two cones pointing up
Two cones pointing down
Two cones base to base
questions.rationale: South: cones down; colours yellow over black.

questions.stem: Red, white, red all-round lights in a vertical line indicate:
options: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel engaged in trawling
A pilot vessel on duty
A vessel not under command
questions.rationale: Rule 27(b)(i) says: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.stem: Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT) is:
options: The level of low water at new moon in any month
The average height of all the low waters in a year
The lowest level predicted under average weather and any astronomical conditions
The lowest tide actually recorded in the last year
questions.rationale: LAT is the lowest predicted tide in a long (about 19-year) cycle.

questions.stem: The shortest distance between two points on the earth's surface is along:
options: A line of constant compass bearing
A great circle
A rhumb line
A parallel of latitude
questions.rationale: A rhumb line is longer except along a meridian or the equator.

questions.stem: CPA means:
options: Computed position accuracy
Collision prevention alert
Course plotted angle
Closest point of approach
questions.rationale: CPA is the minimum predicted distance between two vessels.

questions.stem: You see one all-round white light at night. The vessel is:
options: A power-driven vessel under 50 m underway
A vessel at anchor under 50 m
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel engaged in mine clearance
questions.rationale: Rule 30: one all-round white light indicates a vessel at anchor under 50 m.

questions.stem: A lee shore is a shore:
options: Facing the open sea in light winds
Towards which the wind is blowing
Protected from the wind by high land
With no rocks or shoals
questions.rationale: Strong onshore winds make it hard to claw off.

questions.stem: Beaufort force 6 is:
options: Moderate breeze, 11 to 16 knots
Near gale, 28 to 33 knots
Fresh breeze, 17 to 21 knots
Strong breeze, 22 to 27 knots
questions.rationale: Force 5 is 17–21 kn, force 7 is 28–33 kn. Answer: Strong breeze, 22 to 27 knots.

questions.stem: Pressure is 20 hPa above the standard 1013 hPa. Compared with predictions, the sea level is likely to be about:
options: 2 m lower
2 m higher
20 cm lower
20 cm higher
questions.rationale: About 1 cm of sea level per hPa, inversely. Answer: 20 cm lower.

questions.stem: A rapid fall in pressure of 6 hPa or more in 3 hours usually means:
options: A sea breeze will develop
Visibility will improve rapidly
Gale-force winds are likely soon
A settled spell is on the way
questions.rationale: A rapid fall indicates a deepening depression.

questions.stem: Under Rule 5, 'all available means' includes:
options: A visual look-out and nothing more
Radar, AIS and VHF where appropriate
A listening watch alone
Radar alone when it is working
questions.rationale: Rule 5 says: Radar, AIS and VHF where appropriate.

questions.stem: True course 230°. Variation 7°W. Deviation 2°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 7° (W variation) = 237°. Magnetic to compass: add 2° (W deviation) = 239°.

questions.stem: Vessels with operational radar must also consider:
options: The age of the radar equipment fitted
The height of the mast carrying the scanner
The number of crew available on watch
The limitations and efficiency of the radar
questions.rationale: Rule 6(b) says: The limitations and efficiency of the radar.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 0445. The secondary port time difference for HW is +45 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 0445 +45 min = 0530.

questions.stem: A drying height is 1.5 m and the height of tide is 3.7 m. The depth of water over it is:
questions.rationale: Depth = height of tide − drying height = 3.7 − 1.5 = 2.2 m.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 0110. The secondary port time difference for HW is -15 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 0110 -15 min = 0055.

questions.stem: Wave height generally increases with:
options: Latitude, season and time of day
Water temperature, depth and salinity
Wind strength, duration and fetch
Tide height, range and period
questions.rationale: Fetch is the distance of open water over which the wind blows.

questions.stem: Which is most likely to cause deviation of the steering compass?
options: A handheld radio or speaker stowed beside it
A paper chart on the chart table
A plastic bucket in the cockpit
A lifejacket in the cockpit locker
questions.rationale: Ferrous items and electrical fields near the compass cause deviation.

questions.stem: In open water, a power-driven vessel and a vessel engaged in fishing are on courses that involve risk of collision. A power-driven vessel is not overtaking. Which vessel keeps out of the way?
options: A vessel engaged in fishing
The faster vessel
A power-driven vessel
The larger vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 18 hierarchy: NUC, then RAM, then fishing, then sailing, then power-driven. A lower-ranked vessel keeps out of the way of a higher-ranked one.

questions.stem: The Rules apply to:
options: Only vessels that are on the high seas
Only commercial vessels of any size
Only vessels of more than 12 m in length
All vessels on the high seas and connected navigable waters
questions.rationale: Rule 1(a) says: All vessels on the high seas and connected navigable waters.

questions.stem: A yacht travels 6 NM in 90 minutes. Her speed is:
options: 9.0 knots
3.0 knots
4.0 knots
6.0 knots
questions.rationale: 6 ÷ 1.5 = 4 kn. Answer: 4.0 knots.

questions.stem: In open water, a power-driven vessel and a sailing vessel are on courses that involve risk of collision. A power-driven vessel is not overtaking. Which vessel keeps out of the way?
options: The larger vessel
The faster vessel
A sailing vessel
A power-driven vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 18 hierarchy: NUC, then RAM, then fishing, then sailing, then power-driven. A lower-ranked vessel keeps out of the way of a higher-ranked one.

questions.stem: If the yacht is holed, the first action is to:
options: Stem the leak, start pumps and prepare to call for help
Ignore it until the cabin floor is flooded
Run the engine at full speed to reach the shore
Open all the seacocks to let the water out
questions.rationale: Stop the ingress and pump. Answer: Stem the leak, start pumps and prepare to call for help.

questions.stem: A cardinal light showing groups of nine quick flashes is:
options: East
West
South
North
questions.rationale: North continuous, east 3, south 6 + long flash, west 9.

questions.stem: In restricted visibility, avoiding action for a vessel forward of the beam by radar should avoid:
options: An alteration of course to starboard at once
An alteration of course to port, unless overtaking
The use of sound signals at any time
A reduction of speed to steerage way
questions.rationale: Rule 19(d)(i) says: An alteration of course to port, unless overtaking.

questions.stem: In a power-driven crossing situation, the vessel with the other on her starboard side shall:
options: Keep out of the way and avoid crossing ahead
Turn to port across the other's bow
Cross ahead of the other at full speed
Stand on and sound one short blast
questions.rationale: Rule 15: the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side shall keep out of the way and, if circumstances admit, avoid crossing ahead.

questions.stem: The 'drift' of a tidal stream is its:
options: Direction, in degrees true
Range, in metres
Duration, in hours
Rate, in knots
questions.rationale: Set = direction; drift (rate) = speed in knots.

questions.stem: Compass course 200°. Deviation 4°E. Variation 8°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: add 4° = 204°. Magnetic to true: subtract 8° = 196°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: A vessel is 'underway' if she is:
options: Not at anchor, made fast to the shore or aground
Using her engine to hold her position
Making way through the water at any speed
Moving over the ground at any speed
questions.rationale: Rule 3(i): underway is not the same as 'making way'.

questions.stem: The four stages of passage planning are:
options: Forecast, route, crew briefing and fuel
Appraisal, provisioning, departure and arrival
Appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring
Planning, plotting, steering and logging
questions.rationale: SOLAS V Regulation 34 and RYA guidance use these four stages.

questions.stem: Which is a factor in determining safe speed?
options: Length of the passage
Time of the next tide
State of visibility
Direction of the next waypoint
questions.rationale: Rule 6(a): visibility, traffic density, manoeuvrability, background light, wind, sea and current, draught against depth.

questions.stem: A sea breeze blows:
options: From land to sea by day in fair weather
From sea to land by day in fair weather
From land to sea at night in winter only
From sea to land at night
questions.rationale: The land heats faster than the sea in the day.

questions.stem: Radiation fog is most likely to form:
options: In the afternoon in summer
In strong winds over the open sea
Ahead of a deepening depression
On clear, calm nights over land near the coast
questions.rationale: It may drift out over coastal waters at dawn.

questions.stem: A bank dries 1.2 m. Your draught is 1.4 m and you want 0.6 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.4 + 0.6 = 2.0 m; add the drying height 1.2 m = 3.2 m.

questions.stem: A three-dimensional GPS fix needs at least:
options: Four satellites
Three satellites
Six satellites
Two satellites
questions.rationale: Four satellites solve for latitude, longitude, altitude and clock error.

questions.stem: What does a vessel aground, under 50 m show? (night)
options: Red, white, red all-round lights in a vertical line
Sidelights and sternlight, or a tricolour at the masthead
Anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights in a vertical line
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 30(d): a vessel aground, under 50 m shows anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: Tropical maritime air over the UK usually brings:
options: Strong easterly winds with hail and thunder in the afternoon
Cold clear days with sharp showers and excellent visibility
Mild moist air, low cloud, drizzle and poor visibility
Hot dry days with haze and light north-easterly winds
questions.rationale: Warm moist air cools over the sea and forms stratus and fog.

questions.stem: Compared with neaps, spring tides usually give:
options: Higher HW, higher LW and weaker streams
Lower HW, higher LW and stronger streams
The same range but earlier streams
Higher HW, lower LW and stronger streams
questions.rationale: Springs have the larger range, so HW is higher, LW lower and streams generally faster.

questions.stem: For a three-bearing fix, the best choice of objects is those whose bearings are:
options: About 180° apart
Within 10° of each other
About 60° apart
Almost in line ahead
questions.rationale: Angles of cut near 60° to 90° minimise the uncertainty.

questions.stem: LPG on a boat is dangerous because it is:
options: Heavier than air and collects in the bilge
Odourless and invisible without a detector
Lighter than air and collects under the deckhead
Stored at too high a pressure
questions.rationale: A gas locker should drain overboard. Answer: Heavier than air and collects in the bilge.

questions.stem: A log measures:
options: Distance off a charted object
Depth of water below the keel
Speed and distance through the water
Speed and distance over the ground
questions.rationale: A GPS gives speed over the ground. Answer: Speed and distance through the water.

questions.stem: By the Rule of Twelfths, how much of the range has risen three hours after LW?
options: One quarter of the range
Three twelfths of the range
One half of the range
Two thirds of the range
questions.rationale: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 twelfths, which is half the range.

questions.stem: A vessel engaged in fishing shows by day:
options: Two cones with their bases together
Two black balls in a vertical line
A black cylinder with a ball above
Two cones with points together
questions.rationale: Rule 26(c)(i) says: Two cones with points together.

questions.stem: You see red over white all-round lights in a vertical line at night. The vessel is:
options: A vessel at anchor under 50 m
A trawler engaged in trawling
A vessel aground, under 50 m
A fishing vessel, not trawling
questions.rationale: Rule 26(c): red over white all-round lights in a vertical line indicates a fishing vessel, not trawling.

questions.stem: Spring tides occur:
options: Only in the spring season
Shortly after new and full moon
Shortly after first and last quarter
When the Moon is farthest from the Earth
questions.rationale: Sun and Moon are in line at new and full moon, so their effects combine, giving the greatest range.

questions.stem: Who must keep clear of a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre?
options: Power-driven vessels only, not sailing vessels
Vessels of less than 20 m in length only
Power-driven, sailing and fishing vessels
Vessels of more than 12 m in length only
questions.rationale: Rule 18 says: Power-driven, sailing and fishing vessels.

questions.stem: A power-driven vessel underway but stopped in restricted visibility sounds:
options: One prolonged blast every 2 minutes
Three short blasts every minute
A gong every 2 minutes
Two prolonged blasts every 2 minutes
questions.rationale: Rule 35(b): two prolonged blasts in succession with about 2 seconds between them, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

questions.stem: Blind pilotage is navigating:
options: By instruments and plotted positions, without visual references
By dead reckoning, without keeping a plot
At night using the lights of the shore only
By following another vessel through the channel
questions.rationale: Use radar, GPS, depth and careful plotting. Answer: By instruments and plotted positions, without visual references.

questions.stem: On a Mercator chart, meridians and parallels appear as:
options: Curved lines
Straight lines that converge to the pole
Concentric circles
Straight lines that cross at right angles
questions.rationale: Rhumb lines are straight on a Mercator chart.

questions.stem: Radar ranges are generally more accurate than radar bearings because:
options: Bearings are always magnetic
Range is affected by the compass
Range is affected by the variation
Bearing accuracy is limited by the beam width
questions.rationale: Use ranges for a fix where possible. Answer: Bearing accuracy is limited by the beam width.

questions.stem: A grab bag contains:
options: Cooking equipment, a stove and spare fuel
Flares, EPIRB or PLB, handheld VHF, water and first aid kit
Spare sails and ropes for the dinghy and tender
Paper charts, the ship's log and the almanac
questions.rationale: It should be near the companionway. Answer: Flares, EPIRB or PLB, handheld VHF, water and first aid kit.

questions.stem: Both vessels are power-driven. A vessel bears 070° relative on your port bow, range closing and the bearing steady. You are:
options: The give-way vessel
The stand-on vessel
Meeting her head-on
Overtaking her
questions.rationale: Rule 15 and 17: she has you on her starboard side, so she keeps clear and you hold your course and speed.

questions.stem: Rule 19 (restricted visibility) applies to vessels that are:
options: Not in sight of one another
In sight of one another in fog
Only power-driven vessels
Only in a traffic scheme
questions.rationale: Rule 19(a) says: Not in sight of one another.

questions.stem: The datum shown on a chart note for GPS positions is usually WGS84. If a chart is on a different datum, you should:
options: Apply the correction stated on the chart
Switch off the GPS and use the log and compass only
Ignore the difference, since it is below GPS accuracy
Apply the correction to the charted depths instead
questions.rationale: Satellite positions may need a shift when plotted on older charts.

questions.stem: Distances on a Mercator chart are measured from:
options: The compass rose
The latitude scale at the side, near the track
Any scale on the chart
The longitude scale at the top or bottom
questions.rationale: One minute of latitude equals one nautical mile; the longitude scale does not measure distance.

questions.stem: LW height 0.4 m, HW height 4.6 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 4 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 4.2 m. After 4 h, 9/12 of the range has risen = 3.15 m. Height = 0.4 + 3.15 = 3.55 m.

questions.stem: Rain clutter on radar is reduced by using:
options: The sea clutter (STC) control
The brilliance control
The rain (FTC) control
The tuning control
questions.rationale: FTC reduces returns from rain. Answer: The rain (FTC) control.

questions.stem: In IALA Region A, the port-hand lateral mark when entering from seaward is:
options: Yellow and spherical
Red with a white band
Red and can-shaped
Green and conical
questions.rationale: Port = red can. Answer: Red and can-shaped.

questions.stem: An emergency wreck marking buoy is coloured:
options: Black and red horizontal bands
Red and white vertical stripes
Blue and yellow vertical stripes
Yellow with a black X
questions.rationale: It has an alternating blue and yellow light if lit.

questions.stem: A vessel constrained by her draught may show:
options: Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
A flashing amber light at the masthead
Two all-round green lights in a vertical line
Red, white and red all-round lights in a line
questions.rationale: Rule 28 says: Three all-round red lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: What does a vessel not under command show? (day)
options: A black cylinder
One black ball in the fore part
Two black balls in a vertical line
Three black balls in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 27(a): a vessel not under command shows two black balls in a vertical line.

questions.stem: What does a vessel constrained by her draught show? (night)
options: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line, plus sidelights and sternlight
Masthead light, sidelights and sternlight
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
Anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 28: a vessel constrained by her draught shows three all-round red lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: True course 180°. Variation 9°W. Deviation 1°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 9° (W variation) = 189°. Magnetic to compass: add 1° (W deviation) = 190°.

questions.stem: A sailing vessel overtakes a power-driven vessel. Who keeps out of the way?
options: The faster vessel only if she is under power
The power-driven vessel, as the lower in rank
The vessel with the wind on her port side
The sailing vessel, as the overtaking vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 13 applies notwithstanding any other rule: any vessel overtaking shall keep out of the way.

questions.stem: In the Northern Hemisphere, surface wind around an anticyclone blows:
options: Clockwise and inwards
Anticlockwise and inwards
Clockwise and outwards
Anticlockwise and outwards
questions.rationale: A high has clockwise outward flow in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.stem: Wind round a headland is often strongest:
options: A short distance off the downwind side of the cape
In the middle of a bay
At the head of a long inlet
Close inshore in the lee of the cape
questions.rationale: Wind curves and accelerates around headlands.

questions.stem: You see one black ball in the fore part by day. The vessel is:
options: A vessel constrained by her draught
A tow longer than 200 m
A vessel aground
A vessel at anchor
questions.rationale: Rule 30(a): one black ball in the fore part indicates a vessel at anchor.

questions.stem: LW height 1.5 m, HW height 3.9 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 5 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 2.4 m. After 5 h, 11/12 of the range has risen = 2.20 m. Height = 1.5 + 2.20 = 3.70 m.

questions.stem: A large 'cocked hat' in a three-bearing fix suggests:
options: An error in the tide table
A charted danger nearby
A perfectly accurate fix
An error in one or more bearings
questions.rationale: A large triangle indicates an error; check the compass and plotting.

questions.stem: What mainly causes the tides?
options: The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun on the oceans
The rotation of the earth's magnetic field
Changes in sea temperature through the month
Prevailing winds pushing water towards the coast
questions.rationale: Tides are produced mainly by lunar and solar gravity acting on the oceans.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 0145. The secondary port time difference for HW is +55 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 0145 +55 min = 0240.

questions.stem: Leeway is greatest when the yacht is:
options: Motoring directly into the wind
Close-hauled in a fresh wind
On a broad reach in light wind
Running downwind under full sail
questions.rationale: A close-hauled boat at slow speed makes the most leeway.

questions.stem: For a gas fire on a cooker you should first:
options: Turn off the gas if safe, then smother with a fire blanket
Throw a bucket of water on the flames at once
Open all the hatches and let the fire burn out
Leave the boat immediately without calling for help
questions.rationale: Remove the fuel, then smother. Answer: Turn off the gas if safe, then smother with a fire blanket.

questions.stem: In open water, a sailing vessel and a vessel not under command are on courses that involve risk of collision. A sailing vessel is not overtaking. Which vessel keeps out of the way?
options: A vessel not under command
A sailing vessel
The larger vessel
The faster vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 18 hierarchy: NUC, then RAM, then fishing, then sailing, then power-driven. A lower-ranked vessel keeps out of the way of a higher-ranked one.

questions.stem: When using an extinguisher, aim at:
options: The smoke
The ceiling above the fire
The top of the flames
The base of the flames
questions.rationale: Target the fuel. Answer: The base of the flames.

questions.stem: A bank dries 0.9 m. Your draught is 1.6 m and you want 1.0 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.6 + 1.0 = 2.6 m; add the drying height 0.9 m = 3.5 m.

questions.stem: An echo sounder normally displays:
options: Depth below chart datum, corrected for the state of tide
Depth below the transducer, unless an offset is set
Depth below the keel always, whatever the offset set
Depth below the surface at high water, from the almanac
questions.rationale: Check the offset setting. Answer: Depth below the transducer, unless an offset is set.

questions.stem: True course 125°. Variation 4°E. Deviation 1°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: subtract 4° (E variation) = 121°. Magnetic to compass: add 1° (W deviation) = 122°.

questions.stem: Compared with the gradient wind, the surface wind over the sea is:
options: Veered by 10–15° and weaker, because of friction
Backed by 10–15° and weaker, because of friction
Veered by 10–15° and stronger, because of friction
The same in direction but stronger
questions.rationale: Friction slows the wind and turns it towards low pressure.

questions.stem: The sounder shows depth below the transducer, which is 0.3 m above the keel. Depth below the keel is:
options: The reading
The reading plus 0.3 m
The reading minus 0.3 m
The reading multiplied by 0.3
questions.rationale: The keel is deeper than the transducer. Answer: The reading minus 0.3 m.

questions.stem: Both vessels are power-driven. A vessel bears 035° relative on your starboard bow, range closing and the bearing steady. You are:
options: The give-way vessel
Overtaking her
Meeting her head-on
The stand-on vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 15: the vessel with the other on her own starboard side keeps out of the way.

questions.stem: Streams are often strongest close to a headland because:
options: The seabed is always shallower there
The flow is squeezed and accelerates round it
The Moon's pull is stronger near land
Chart datum is lower near headlands
questions.rationale: Headlands constrict the flow; overfalls and eddies often form.

questions.stem: LW height 1.5 m, HW height 6.9 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 5 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 5.4 m. After 5 h, 11/12 of the range has risen = 4.95 m. Height = 1.5 + 4.95 = 6.45 m.

questions.stem: A red parachute flare signals:
options: Fog
Safe arrival
Distress
Trawling
questions.rationale: Red parachute and hand flares are distress signals.

questions.stem: Local harbour rules:
options: Apply in their area but must conform as closely as possible to the IRPCS
Never apply to yachts of any size
Always override the IRPCS in their area
Apply to commercial vessels only
questions.rationale: Rule 1(b) says: Apply in their area but must conform as closely as possible to the IRPCS.

questions.stem: What does a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre show? (night)
options: Red, white, red all-round lights in a vertical line
Sidelights and sternlight, or a tricolour at the masthead
One all-round white light
White over red all-round lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 27(b): a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shows red, white, red all-round lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: At 4.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 36 NM?
options: 8 h 00 min
10 h 17 min
6 h 33 min
0 h 08 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 36 ÷ 4.5 = 8.00 h = 8 h 00 min.

questions.stem: In a crossing situation the give-way vessel should avoid:
options: Altering course to starboard
Crossing ahead of the other vessel
Reducing speed
Stopping her engine
questions.rationale: Rule 15 says: Crossing ahead of the other vessel.

questions.stem: At 4.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 14 NM?
options: 4 h 00 min
0 h 19 min
2 h 33 min
3 h 07 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 14 ÷ 4.5 = 3.11 h = 3 h 07 min.

questions.stem: The VHF distress, safety and calling channel is:
options: Channel 70
Channel 16
Channel 12
Channel 6
questions.rationale: Channel 70 is reserved for DSC. Answer: Channel 16.

questions.stem: At 7.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 33 NM?
options: 5 h 05 min
4 h 24 min
0 h 14 min
3 h 53 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 33 ÷ 7.5 = 4.40 h = 4 h 24 min.

questions.stem: Under Rule 18, a power-driven vessel underway keeps out of the way of all of these EXCEPT:
options: A vessel not under command
A sailing vessel
A seaplane on the water
A vessel engaged in fishing
questions.rationale: Rule 18(a) lists NUC, RAM, fishing and sailing vessels; seaplanes shall keep well clear of all vessels (Rule 18(e)).

questions.stem: To make good 000° against a stream setting 090° at 2 kn with boat speed 5 kn, you must steer:
options: Due north
Due west
East of north, about 024°
West of north, about 336°
questions.rationale: Steer up-tide of the desired track: sin⁻¹(2/5) ≈ 24° to the west of north.

questions.stem: ETA is calculated as:
options: Time now plus boat speed divided by distance
Time now plus distance to go multiplied by speed
Time now plus distance to go divided by speed over ground
Time now plus distance to go divided by wind speed
questions.rationale: Adjust for the tide expected along the route.

questions.stem: Three short blasts mean:
options: I am operating astern propulsion
I intend to anchor
I am altering course to starboard
I am in distress
questions.rationale: Rule 34(a): three short blasts = operating astern propulsion.

questions.stem: A PLB is:
options: A handheld VHF radio
A type of lifejacket light
A vessel's fixed distress beacon
A personal beacon carried by an individual
questions.rationale: It is not a substitute for a vessel EPIRB. Answer: A personal beacon carried by an individual.

questions.stem: A liferaft should be serviced:
options: Only after it has been inflated and used
Only when it has been repacked by the owner
At intervals set by the manufacturer, by an approved station
Once every ten years, when the yacht is surveyed
questions.rationale: Typically annually or every three years. Answer: At intervals set by the manufacturer, by an approved station.

questions.stem: After the passage of a cold front over the UK, the wind typically veers from:
options: South-west to north-west
North-east to south-east
South-east to north-east
North to south
questions.rationale: The change is clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.stem: Katabatic winds are:
options: Cold, dense air flowing downhill, usually at night
Warm air flowing uphill on sunny days
Gusts from thunderstorms
Winds blowing around a high
questions.rationale: They are gravity-driven down-slope flows. Answer: Cold, dense air flowing downhill, usually at night.

questions.stem: Why must GPS never be your only means of navigation?
options: It cannot show the position of a headland
It can fail, be jammed or be mis-set, so cross-check it
It does not work in the dark
It is not legal for use offshore
questions.rationale: Always have independent checks. Answer: It can fail, be jammed or be mis-set, so cross-check it.

questions.stem: A sign of developing hypothermia is:
options: Sweating and a flushed face with a fast pulse
Hunger and restlessness with a cold nose
A high pulse and thirst with a dry mouth
Shivering, followed by confusion and slurred speech
questions.rationale: Treat gently. Answer: Shivering, followed by confusion and slurred speech.

questions.stem: An occluded front forms when:
options: A cold front overtakes a warm front
A ridge builds in behind a trough
Two cold fronts meet over the sea
A warm front overtakes a cold front
questions.rationale: The cold front moves faster and lifts the warm sector.

questions.stem: Spring range 5.0 m, neap range 2.0 m. Today's range is 3.5 m. The tide is:
options: Half-way between springs and neaps
Neaps, since the range is nearer the neap range
Springs, since the range is nearer the spring range
Abnormally high, because of a storm surge
questions.rationale: 3.5 m is the mid-point of 2.0 m and 5.0 m. Answer: Half-way between springs and neaps.

questions.stem: Sea clutter on radar is reduced by using:
options: The rain (FTC) control
The sea clutter (STC) control
The gain at maximum
The range control
questions.rationale: Too much STC may hide small targets. Answer: The sea clutter (STC) control.

questions.stem: You plan to round a headland with a race. The safest time is usually:
options: Just after the stream turns against you
At the strongest part of the stream
At or near slack water, or with the stream
When wind is against the stream
questions.rationale: Races are worst with wind against tide and at springs.

questions.stem: LW height 1.0 m, HW height 4.6 m. Using the Rule of Twelfths, what is the height of tide 5 hours after LW?
questions.rationale: Range 3.6 m. After 5 h, 11/12 of the range has risen = 3.30 m. Height = 1.0 + 3.30 = 4.30 m.

questions.stem: You see green over white all-round lights in a vertical line at night. The vessel is:
options: A fishing vessel, not trawling
A trawler engaged in trawling
A vessel not under command, making way
A vessel at anchor under 50 m
questions.rationale: Rule 26(b): green over white all-round lights in a vertical line indicates a trawler engaged in trawling.

questions.stem: AIS should be used:
options: To decide right of way automatically
To supplement, not replace, a visual look-out
To replace a visual look-out at night
As the sole means of avoiding collision
questions.rationale: AIS may not show all vessels. Answer: To supplement, not replace, a visual look-out.

questions.stem: Two position lines crossing at 90° give a fix that is:
options: Less reliable than lines crossing at 20°
Reliable only with three lines
More reliable than lines crossing at 20°
Exactly as reliable as lines crossing at 20°
questions.rationale: A better angle of cut reduces the uncertainty from bearing errors.

questions.stem: A critical hazard on the route is best passed:
options: At low water, so as to see the hazard on the chart
In fog, so as to avoid crowds of other vessels
In the dark, so that the lights of the hazard are seen
In daylight and good visibility where possible
questions.rationale: Plan the timing of difficult sections. Answer: In daylight and good visibility where possible.

questions.stem: A bank dries 2.1 m. Your draught is 1.6 m and you want 0.5 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.6 + 0.5 = 2.1 m; add the drying height 2.1 m = 4.2 m.

questions.stem: True course 100°. Variation 2°W. Deviation 5°E. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 2° (W variation) = 102°. Magnetic to compass: subtract 5° (E deviation) = 097°.

questions.stem: Each sidelight shows over an arc of:
questions.rationale: Rule 21(b): from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam.

questions.stem: Planning fuel for a passage, you should:
options: Count only the hours under engine in harbour
Refuel only after arrival
Allow a reserve for delays and adverse conditions
Carry the exact amount calculated
questions.rationale: A rule of thumb is one third out, one third back, one third reserve.

questions.stem: A ridge of high pressure is usually associated with:
options: Fair, settled weather and light winds
Heavy frontal rain and a steadily backing wind
Gales and a rapidly falling barometer ahead of a front
Rapid falls of pressure with squalls and thunder
questions.rationale: Ridges bring subsidence and clearing skies. Answer: Fair, settled weather and light winds.

questions.stem: You see masthead light, sidelights and sternlight at night. The vessel is:
options: A sailing vessel underway
A power-driven vessel under 50 m underway
A pilot vessel on duty
A vessel aground, under 50 m
questions.rationale: Rule 23: masthead light, sidelights and sternlight indicates a power-driven vessel under 50 m underway.

questions.stem: A no-go area marked on the chart is used to:
options: Show where speed limits begin and end in a harbour
Show the limit of VHF range from the coast station
Show the preferred anchorages along the route
Show water to be avoided given draught and tide
questions.rationale: Mark clear no-go areas and clearing lines near hazards.

questions.stem: A jackstay is:
options: A line to the dinghy kept on the transom
A line or strap along the deck for clipping on
A type of storm sail set on the inner forestay
A restraint line to hold the boom in position
questions.rationale: It allows movement along the deck while clipped on.

questions.stem: The characteristic Fl(3) 15s means:
options: Three flashes, each lasting 15 seconds
A group of three flashes in every 15 seconds
A flash every 3 seconds for 15 seconds
Three lights flashing every 15 seconds
questions.rationale: Fl(3) = group of 3 flashes; 15s is the period of the cycle.

questions.stem: A sailing vessel under sail and engine together is treated as:
options: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel not under command
A sailing vessel
A power-driven vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 3(b): 'power-driven vessel' means any vessel propelled by machinery.

questions.stem: The geographical range of a light depends on:
options: The height of the light and the observer's height of eye
The height of the tide at the light and the observer
The state of the weather at the light and in between
The brightness of the lamp and the clarity of the air
questions.rationale: It is limited by the curvature of the earth. Answer: The height of the light and the observer's height of eye.

questions.stem: An estimated position (EP) is a DR position that has also been corrected for:
options: Tidal stream and leeway
Wind speed and direction
Variation and deviation
Magnetic compass error
questions.rationale: EP = DR + stream + leeway. Answer: Tidal stream and leeway.

questions.stem: A standard port is a port for which:
options: Daily predictions of tide times and heights are published
Predictions are given as differences from a nearby port
A tide gauge is installed on the quay
Only the times of HW are published
questions.rationale: Secondary ports get theirs by applying differences to a standard port.

questions.stem: A low-pressure system passes. Compared with predictions, the actual height of tide is likely to be:
options: Lower than predicted
Higher than predicted
Unchanged
Higher at LW only
questions.rationale: Low pressure lets sea level rise, about 1 cm per hPa below standard pressure.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 0940. The secondary port time difference for HW is +45 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 0940 +45 min = 1025.

questions.stem: Two power-driven vessels meet head-on with risk of collision. Each shall:
options: Alter course to port
Alter course to starboard only if smaller
Alter course to starboard
Hold course and reduce speed
questions.rationale: Rule 14(a): each shall alter course to starboard so that each passes on the port side of the other.

questions.stem: Compass course 210°. Deviation 3°E. Variation 5°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: add 3° = 213°. Magnetic to true: subtract 5° = 208°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: Your vessel's MMSI is:
options: The owner's telephone number, as registered ashore
A nine-digit number identifying the vessel for DSC and AIS
A call sign made up of letters and a number
The vessel's registered tonnage, as on her certificate
questions.rationale: It is entered into the radio and AIS. Answer: A nine-digit number identifying the vessel for DSC and AIS.

questions.stem: At 6.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 36 NM?
options: 5 h 32 min
4 h 48 min
0 h 11 min
6 h 33 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 36 ÷ 6.5 = 5.54 h = 5 h 32 min.

questions.stem: A stream sets 270° at 3 kn. You steer 000° at 6 kn. In one hour the stream displaces you from your DR position by:
options: 3 NM towards 000°
3 NM towards 270°
9 NM towards 270°
6 NM towards 270°
questions.rationale: The stream moves you its drift in the hour, whatever your heading.

questions.stem: For an unresponsive casualty who is not breathing normally:
options: Give a drink and monitor
Call for help and start chest compressions
Wait for the coastguard before acting
Put them in a bunk to rest
questions.rationale: Start CPR at once. Answer: Call for help and start chest compressions.

questions.stem: At 4.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 8 NM?
options: 1 h 27 min
1 h 47 min
2 h 17 min
0 h 34 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 8 ÷ 4.5 = 1.78 h = 1 h 47 min.

questions.stem: Why lift a cold, exhausted casualty horizontally if possible?
options: To keep their clothes dry
To make them easier to hold
To reduce the risk of rescue collapse
To reduce rope wear
questions.rationale: Vertical lifting can drop blood pressure. Answer: To reduce the risk of rescue collapse.

questions.stem: Deviation is the angle between:
options: True north and compass north
Magnetic north and compass north
The track and the heading
True north and magnetic north
questions.rationale: Deviation is caused by the vessel's own magnetic fields and changes with heading.

questions.stem: Standard sea-level pressure is approximately:
options: 980 hPa
1100 hPa
1013 hPa
1050 hPa
questions.rationale: Standard pressure at sea level is 1013.25 hPa.

questions.stem: A pilot vessel on duty at night shows:
options: Green over green all-round lights
White over red all-round lights
Two all-round white lights
Red over white all-round lights
questions.rationale: Rule 29(a)(i) says: White over red all-round lights.

questions.stem: A land breeze blows:
options: From sea to land at dawn only
From land to sea at midday
From land to sea at night
From sea to land at night
questions.rationale: The land cools faster than the sea at night. Answer: From land to sea at night.

questions.stem: A masthead light shows over an arc of:
questions.rationale: Rule 21(a): from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam on each side.

questions.stem: What does a vessel engaged in fishing show? (day)
options: Two black cones with their points together
Two black balls in a vertical line
One black ball in the fore part
A diamond on tug and tow
questions.rationale: Rule 26: a vessel engaged in fishing shows two black cones with their points together.

questions.stem: Buys Ballot's law: in the Northern Hemisphere, with your back to the wind, low pressure is:
options: On your right
Directly behind you
Directly ahead
On your left
questions.rationale: Back to the wind, low pressure lies to the left.

questions.stem: A vessel under 50 m aground shows at night:
options: Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
Anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights
Red over white over red all-round lights
Green over red all-round lights
questions.rationale: Rule 30(d) says: Anchor light(s) and two all-round red lights.

questions.stem: The Rule of Twelfths assumes that in successive hours the tide changes by:
options: 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1 twelfths of the range
2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 twelfths of the range
3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1 twelfths of the range
1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 twelfths of the range
questions.rationale: The rule approximates a regular curve of about six hours between HW and LW.

questions.stem: At 7.5 kn over the ground, how long to cover 36 NM?
options: 5 h 32 min
0 h 12 min
4 h 14 min
4 h 48 min
questions.rationale: Time = distance ÷ speed = 36 ÷ 7.5 = 4.80 h = 4 h 48 min.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 1310. The secondary port time difference for HW is -45 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 1310 -45 min = 1225.

questions.stem: HW at the standard port is 1915. The secondary port time difference for HW is -15 minutes. What is the time of HW at the secondary port?
questions.rationale: Add the signed difference: 1915 -15 min = 1900.

questions.stem: In IALA Region A, the starboard-hand lateral mark when entering from seaward is:
options: Yellow and spherical
Green and conical
Red and can-shaped
Green with a red band
questions.rationale: Port = red can; starboard = green cone. Answer: Green and conical.

questions.stem: A vessel crossing a traffic lane should, so far as practicable, steer:
options: Parallel to the nearest edge of the lane
On the same heading as the nearest ship
At right angles to the general traffic flow
At as shallow an angle as possible to the flow
questions.rationale: Rule 10(c): cross traffic lanes on a heading at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow.

questions.stem: A dan buoy and light is used to:
options: Mark the position of a person in the water
Signal your ETA to the harbour
Mark the anchor position
Measure the height of tide
questions.rationale: It stays visible while you manoeuvre. Answer: Mark the position of a person in the water.

questions.stem: Action to avoid collision under Rule 8 should be:
options: Made in small steps so the other vessel can follow
Delayed until the other vessel has acted first
Confined to a reduction in speed whenever possible
Large enough to be readily apparent to the other vessel
questions.rationale: Rule 8(b): any alteration of course or speed shall be large enough to be readily apparent; a succession of small alterations should be avoided.

questions.stem: Navigation lights shall be shown:
options: From dusk to dawn only, if the vessel is under way
At night only, and only when in a channel
From sunset to sunrise, and in restricted visibility by day
Only when other vessels are known to be near
questions.rationale: Rule 20(a) says: From sunset to sunrise, and in restricted visibility by day.

questions.stem: Beaufort force 4 is:
options: Fresh breeze, 17 to 21 knots
Moderate breeze, 11 to 16 knots
Gentle breeze, 7 to 10 knots
Light breeze, 4 to 6 knots
questions.rationale: Force 4 = 11–16 kn. Answer: Moderate breeze, 11 to 16 knots.

questions.stem: Orange smoke is a distress signal for use:
options: In fog only
At night
In harbour only
In daylight
questions.rationale: At night use red flares. Answer: In daylight.

questions.stem: A vessel on a steady compass bearing with decreasing range indicates:
options: She will pass clear ahead
She is moving at the same speed
Risk of collision exists
She will pass clear astern
questions.rationale: Rule 7(d): if the compass bearing of an approaching vessel does not appreciably change, risk of collision shall be deemed to exist.

questions.stem: Swell is:
options: Short, steep waves raised by the local wind in the area
Waves that have travelled out of the area where they were raised
Waves that are breaking in shallow water near a beach
Waves raised by the tidal stream running over shallows
questions.rationale: Swell is long-period, regular and outlives the wind that made it.

questions.stem: A leading line is marked by:
options: A fixed anchor laid at the end of the pier
Two buoys moored side by side in the channel
Two beacons or lights that appear in line on the safe track
A single red buoy at the entrance to the channel
questions.rationale: Keep them in line. Answer: Two beacons or lights that appear in line on the safe track.

questions.stem: A trough of low pressure usually brings:
options: Persistent clear skies and light winds
Showers or rain and a veer of wind
Steady easterly winds
Fog and no change in wind
questions.rationale: Troughs behave like weak fronts. Answer: Showers or rain and a veer of wind.

questions.stem: What does a fishing vessel, not trawling show? (night)
options: Red, white, red all-round lights in a vertical line
Masthead light, sidelights and sternlight
Red over white all-round lights in a vertical line
Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
questions.rationale: Rule 26(c): a fishing vessel, not trawling shows red over white all-round lights in a vertical line.

questions.stem: A passage of 24 NM at 4.5 kn boat speed has an average fair stream of 1.5 kn. The time taken is:
options: 5 hours 20 minutes
3 hours
6 hours
4 hours
questions.rationale: SOG = 6 kn; 24 ÷ 6 = 4 h. Answer: 4 hours.

questions.stem: A departure from the Rules is permitted:
options: When it saves time
When the other vessel is smaller
To avoid immediate danger
Only in a traffic scheme
questions.rationale: Rule 2(b) says: To avoid immediate danger.

questions.stem: A low HDOP on a GPS indicates:
options: A strong tidal stream running at the receiver position
Poor satellite geometry and a less accurate fix
Good satellite geometry for horizontal position
A loss of the compass heading input to the receiver
questions.rationale: Higher HDOP means a less accurate fix. Answer: Good satellite geometry for horizontal position.

questions.stem: A drying height of 1.8 m on a chart means the seabed there is:
options: 1.8 m below chart datum
1.8 m below the surface at HW
1.8 m above chart datum
1.8 m above mean high water
questions.rationale: Drying heights are underlined figures measured above chart datum.

questions.stem: LW height 0.8 m, HW 6.8 m. By the Rule of Twelfths, the height 4 hours after LW is:
