questions.stem: A bank dries 1.5 m. Your draught is 1.8 m and you want 0.6 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.8 + 0.6 = 2.4 m; add the drying height 1.5 m = 3.9 m.

questions.stem: A secondary port's tide times and heights are found by:
options: Reading a tidal diamond on the chart
Applying differences to a standard port's predictions
Interpolating between two other secondary ports
Using the Rule of Twelfths from chart datum
questions.rationale: Differences are tabulated in the almanac against a standard port.

questions.stem: Under Rule 6, a safe speed allows the vessel to:
options: Stay below the engine's maximum rated revolutions
Stop within a distance appropriate to the conditions
Reach the next harbour before it gets dark
Hold steerage way whatever the conditions
questions.rationale: Rule 6: take proper and effective action to avoid collision and be stopped within a distance appropriate to the prevailing circumstances.

questions.stem: A tidal stream 'setting 075°' flows:
options: At 075 knots
From 075°
Towards 075°
At 075 degrees to the wind
questions.rationale: The set is the direction towards which the stream flows; wind direction is the opposite convention.

questions.stem: For close inshore pilotage use:
options: The smallest scale chart available
The largest scale chart available
An ocean passage chart
A route planning chart
questions.rationale: Large-scale charts show hazards in detail. Answer: The largest scale chart available.

questions.stem: The characteristic Iso 4s means:
options: A light visible for 4 miles
Light for 4 seconds then dark for 4 seconds
Four flashes in every cycle
Equal periods of light and dark, a cycle of 4 seconds
questions.rationale: Isophase: light and dark durations are equal; the whole period is 4 seconds.

questions.stem: In the Shipping Forecast, 'good' visibility means:
options: More than 10 nautical miles
More than 2 nautical miles
More than 1 nautical mile
More than 5 nautical miles
questions.rationale: Good > 5 NM; moderate 2–5 NM; poor 1000 m–2 NM; fog < 1000 m.

questions.stem: A bank dries 0.6 m. Your draught is 1.2 m and you want 0.5 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.2 + 0.5 = 1.7 m; add the drying height 0.6 m = 2.3 m.

questions.stem: You see white over red all-round lights in a vertical line at night. The vessel is:
options: A power-driven vessel under 50 m underway
A pilot vessel on duty
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel constrained by her draught
questions.rationale: Rule 29: white over red all-round lights in a vertical line indicates a pilot vessel on duty.

questions.stem: You see ball, diamond, ball in a vertical line by day. The vessel is:
options: A vessel engaged in fishing
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A vessel not under command
A tow longer than 200 m
questions.rationale: Rule 27(b): ball, diamond, ball in a vertical line indicates a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.stem: At night you see a vessel's red sidelight on your port bow, bearing steady, range closing. She and you are both power-driven. You should:
options: Sound five blasts and stop
Alter to port as the give-way vessel
Hold course and speed as the stand-on vessel
Alter to starboard as the give-way vessel
questions.rationale: A red light is her port side, so she has you on her starboard side and must give way (Rule 15).

questions.stem: On a leading line, the rear mark appears to the right of the front mark. You are:
options: On the line
To the right of the line, so alter to starboard
To the left of the line, so alter to port
To the left of the line, so alter to starboard
questions.rationale: Steer towards the side the rear mark is displaced.

questions.stem: True course 030°. Variation 4°W. Deviation 3°W. What is the compass course?
questions.rationale: True to magnetic: add 4° (W variation) = 034°. Magnetic to compass: add 3° (W deviation) = 037°.

questions.stem: Standard MHWS 5.6 m, secondary height difference −0.9 m. MHWS at the secondary port is:
Three red lights in a vertical line at a harbour signal station normally mean:
options: Traffic is one-way
Small craft only may enter
Entry is free
Entry is prohibited
questions.rationale: Check the local signals in the pilot book. Answer: Entry is prohibited.

questions.stem: You see three all-round green lights at night. The vessel is:
options: A vessel at anchor under 50 m
A vessel engaged in mine clearance
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
A power-driven vessel under 50 m underway
questions.rationale: Rule 27(f): three all-round green lights indicates a vessel engaged in mine clearance.

questions.stem: A north cardinal mark has the topmark:
options: Two cones pointing up
Two cones pointing down
Two cones base to base
Two cones point to point
questions.rationale: North: both cones up; colours black over yellow.

questions.stem: Who must keep clear of a vessel not under command?
options: All vessels
Only sailing vessels
Only power-driven vessels
Only vessels over 50 m
questions.rationale: Rule 18 says: All vessels.

questions.stem: A towing light is:
options: Red, flashing at 120 flashes a minute
White, with an all-round arc of 360 degrees
Yellow, with the arc of a sternlight
Green, with an all-round arc of 360 degrees
questions.rationale: Rule 21(d) says: Yellow, with the arc of a sternlight.

questions.stem: Before entering an unfamiliar harbour you should:
options: Study the large-scale chart and pilot book and identify marks
Approach at full speed so as to keep control of the boat
Follow the first vessel you see go in ahead of you
Enter at night to avoid the busy daytime traffic
questions.rationale: Preparation reduces risk. Answer: Study the large-scale chart and pilot book and identify marks.

questions.stem: Compass course 355°. Deviation 5°W. Variation 9°W. What is the true course?
questions.rationale: Compass to magnetic: subtract 5° = 350°. Magnetic to true: subtract 9° = 341°. (Cadet: Compass → add East → True.)

questions.stem: A bank dries 1.2 m. Your draught is 1.8 m and you want 0.6 m under the keel. What height of tide is the minimum needed to cross it?
questions.rationale: Water needed over the bank = 1.8 + 0.6 = 2.4 m; add the drying height 1.2 m = 3.6 m.
